name: MA-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strong Democratic district lean (D+6 PVI) plus a favorable national environment
Incumbent Bill Keating running with a large cash advantage over Tyler MacAllister
Prediction markets price Democratic win at roughly 96%
No general-election polls, so the forecast rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The fundamentals point firmly to Keating: a D+6 district, incumbency, a favorable environment, and a fundraising edge of nearly half a million dollars in cash on hand over his Republican challenger. Markets price this race as a near-certain Democratic hold, and nothing in the evidence suggests movement away from that picture.
model.watch: A late surge in Republican spending or polling showing an unexpectedly competitive race would be the main signals to revisit.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Massachusetts' 9th District sits in Cape Cod and the South Shore, and its Democratic lean of about six points gives incumbent Bill Keating a solid structural advantage. Keating is running for reelection with roughly $495,000 on hand, while Republican Tyler MacAllister has raised far less and holds about $35,000. No outside groups are active in the race, and no expert raters list it as competitive.

Prediction markets put the Democratic chance of holding the seat near 96%. With no general-election polling available, the forecast leans on fundamentals, which all point the same direction: district lean, incumbency, money, and a favorable national environment for Democrats. The race is rated Safe D, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of direct polling rather than any sign of a genuine contest.
